title: For such a time as this (Esther 4:14)
hookLine: "who knoweth whether thou art not come to royal estate for such a time as this?"
carry: the strange road that brought her here

cards: The news reaches the queen secondhand. Her maids tell Esther that Mordecai is outside the king's gate in sackcloth and ashes.
In every province the decree has reached, the text says, there's mourning among the Jews, fasting and weeping. Esther sends Mordecai clothes; he won't put them on.
So messages go back and forth through a servant named Hatach. Mordecai sends a copy of the decree and asks her to plead with the king for her people. Esther's answer is careful, and true.
Anyone who enters the inner court uncalled is put to death, unless the king holds out his golden scepter. And she hasn't been called, she says, for thirty days. Mordecai's answer ends in a question.

teach.b: He starts bluntly. In the King James words: "Think not with thyself that thou shalt escape in the king's house, more than all the Jews." The palace walls won't hide her.

teach.h: HELP WILL COME FROM ANOTHER PLACE.
teach.b: If she stays silent, help will still come to the Jews, from another place. Mordecai doesn't think the rescue depends on her alone.

teach.h: WHO KNOWETH: A QUESTION, NOT A PROMISE.
teach.b: The question is whether she'll be part of it.

teach.h: FOR SUCH A TIME AS THIS.
teach.b: Then, in the 1917 Jewish translation: "who knoweth whether thou art not come to royal estate for such a time as this?" Notice it's a question. Who knows.
Mordecai doesn't promise it will work. He doesn't tell her she was born for this.

teach.h: THE HIDDEN QUEEN, IN THE RIGHT ROOM.
teach.b: He only asks her to consider that the strange road that brought her here, the orphan raised by her cousin, the girl taken into the palace, the queen who kept her people a secret, might have been leading to this one moment.
The thing that kept her safe and quiet is the very thing that gives her a voice now. Some readers linger on that phrase, from another place.
Esther is a story where help arrives through ordinary people, timing and nerve, and some hear in another place a quiet hint of God. Others hear simply that the people will survive somehow.
Either way, the question lands on Esther.

how: Esther 9:22 names how the days of Purim are to be kept, with feasting and joy, sending portions one to another, and gifts to the poor, and Purim is still kept with a festive meal, gifts of food to friends, and gifts to the poor.

the queen's high position, reached for this moment

s: Mordecai promises Esther that she will succeed
he asks a question: who knoweth. there's no promise.

games.q: you're Esther. your people are in danger, and going to the king uncalled could cost your life. you tell Mordecai so. what does he send back?
o: stay quiet; the palace will keep you safe.
help may come from elsewhere, but maybe this is why you're here.
wait until the king calls for you.
games.why: he tells her the palace won't hide her, that help can come from another place, and asks: who knoweth whether thou art not come to royal estate for such a time as this?

practice: Walk in your mind through the places you'll stand this week, a desk, a kitchen, a phone, a family, and see whether one of them holds one thing you're placed to say or do: not the whole rescue, just a word to the right person.
Don't decide yet; just set Mordecai's question beside it: who knows whether you're here for this. If you pray, bring it to God in words from your tradition, or in silence.

wordCard.voice: Royal estate. Mordecai's question to Esther: who knows whether she came to royal estate for such a time as this. Today's word.
